title: 01  Plate layout and electronic identity audit
caption: All 96 raw sample IDs match both the run manifest and the experiment layout. There are 72 DNA wells and 24 A31 buffer blanks. Original concentration metadata uses 16 ng/µL for A30; this map uses the user-corrected 70 ng/µL stock and nominal twofold dilutions. Electronic agreement does not independently prove physical contents.

title: 02  Raw and corrected readings retain every well
caption: All 96 readings are finite. Raw A260 ranges from 0.05649 to 0.53148 OD. Each well is corrected with its own volume's blank mean. D9 is outlined for follow-up, not excluded. Neither heatmap measures actual fill volumes.

title: 03  The 50 µL DNA-run blanks are quiet
caption: Blank SDs are 0.000330, 0.001054, 0.001046 and 0.002242 OD at 50, 75, 100 and 200 µL. The high 50 µL background seen in the earlier Orange G run is absent here. This is a different preparation and wavelength; it does not identify the cause of the earlier problem.

title: 04  Concentration-response curves at each volume
caption: Responses rise strongly with nominal concentration at every volume. Full-range R² values are high, but this alone does not establish strict linearity or low-end accuracy. Fit all 18 sample wells per panel with a free intercept; the residual analysis shows where a straight line misses group means.

title: 05  Detecting a signal is different from precise measurement
caption: All three 2.1875 ng/µL wells at each volume exceed the matching 3.3-blank-SD screen. Their corrected CVs are 100.5%, 18.9%, 8.5% and 8.0% as volume increases. Thus a favorable blank-noise ratio at 50 µL does not rescue its inconsistent low-concentration samples. Thresholds are exploratory screens, not validated detection probabilities.

title: 06  Signal generally increases with well volume
caption: At fixed concentration, larger planned volumes generally give larger corrected absorbance. The lowest concentration is disrupted by the elevated D9 result at 50 µL. At 2.1875 ng/µL, moving from 100 to 200 µL nearly doubles mean signal, but blank variability also increases, so signal gain alone is not a detection-limit improvement.

title: 07  Precision favors 100 µL at the lowest tested concentration
caption: At 100 and 200 µL, all six concentrations have within-condition corrected CV below 10%. At 75 µL, 2.1875 and 4.375 ng/µL have CVs of 18.9% and 12.9%. At 50 µL, CV is below 10% from 8.75 to 70 ng/µL, but fails badly at 2.1875 ng/µL. These three-well CVs measure within-plate repeatability, not dilution accuracy or between-day precision.

title: 08  Blank noise and sample precision must be considered together
caption: The 50 µL, 2.1875 ng/µL mean is 31.7 blank SD above zero, yet its CV is 100.5%. In contrast, 100 µL gives a smaller ratio of 8.24 but much tighter samples. The blank-noise ratio is not instrument signal-to-noise and is not a substitute for repeatable sample results or accuracy validation.

title: 09  Noise-based limits are hypotheses to validate
caption: Full-range blank-noise DL estimates are approximately 0.73, 1.44, 1.02 and 1.12 ng/µL; QL estimates are 2.22, 4.35, 3.09 and 3.40 ng/µL. The apparently favorable 50 µL DL conflicts with its low-end sample variability. The fixed 2.1875-17.5 ng/µL fits show range sensitivity. Values below 2.1875 ng/µL were not tested, and neither these intervals nor high R² establish a validated limit.

title: 10  Volume normalization diagnoses departures from simple scaling
caption: Most volume-normalized responses are close to the 100 µL reference, particularly at moderate concentrations. The 50 µL, 2.1875 ng/µL point is elevated and uncertain because D9 raises its mean. Dividing by planned volume is a descriptive normalization, not a measured path-length correction or evidence of actual dispensed volume.

title: 11  High R² does not rule out systematic departures
caption: Red group means have 95% bootstrap departure intervals that exclude zero. Several conditions depart detectably from their fitted lines despite high R². These are exploratory, unadjusted comparisons based on one plate. They can reflect optical response, dilution error, dispensing differences or isolated wells; they do not isolate a mechanism.

title: 12  Spatial checks locate influential wells without assigning causes
caption: D9 is conspicuous within its own concentration-volume condition. Spatial residuals also identify the strongest discrepancies elsewhere, but each location has only one observation and variance changes with signal. A single map cannot distinguish a positional optical effect from pipetting, dilution or a bubble. All wells remain included.

title: 13  D9 drives the largest low-volume inconsistency
caption: At 50 µL and 2.1875 ng/µL, A8, C10 and D9 read 0.005148, 0.003658 and 0.022558 OD after subtraction. The three-well CV is 100.5%. Omitting D9 only as a sensitivity calculation leaves two wells with CV 23.9%, still uncertain. D9 has no documented physical exclusion reason and is retained in every primary result.

title: 14  Minimum concentration and minimum sample mass are different goals
caption: At the lowest tested concentration of 2.1875 ng/µL, the wells contain nominally 109.375, 164.063, 218.75 and 437.5 ng at increasing volumes. The 100 µL condition resolves that level with 8.5% within-plate CV using 218.75 ng. Reducing volume saves DNA but reduces optical signal and can expose dispensing or meniscus variability. Actual DNA mass was not independently measured.

title: 15  Volume-response residuals expose departures from a line
caption: The 35 ng/µL series has an exploratory departure at 200 µL; the 70 ng/µL series has departures at 50, 100 and 200 µL. Lower-concentration series show no clear group departure by this conditional interval rule. The lowest concentration remains imprecise because of D9; absence of a clear departure is not proof of linearity.
